solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Huge region over in USA is Appalachia

indicators.note: over in a clue tells the solver to turn the found letters back to front
in says the letters sit inside the run of words USA is Appalachia

explanation.surface: A geography note claiming the Appalachian region of the USA is vast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds AISA inside 'USA is Appalachia', and 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent is a straightforward example of a huge region of the world.

clue.text: Solid coach up street and against centre of driveway

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for coach is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a coach is a bus
anti means against

indicators.note: centre of picks the two middle letters of driveway

explanation.surface: A sturdy coach is backed up a street against the middle of a driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses BUS to SUB; 'centre of' gives VE from driveway.
explanation.definitionFit: Something substantial and firmly real, having substance, is solid in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Lark circling seaman on cape in coldest area

indicators.note: circling means the word for lark wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a lark is a prank, as is an antic

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the sailor above the cape

parts.note: tar is old slang for a sailor
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A songbird circles a sailor on a headland in polar waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lark' is not the bird but a prank, an antic.
explanation.definitionFit: The south polar region is the coldest place on Earth.

clue.text: Spar put in advertisement for email manager

indicators.note: put in tells us the spar is placed inside the advertisement

parts.note: a poster is a printed advertisement on a wall
a spar is a pole on a ship, such as a mast

explanation.surface: Instructions to place a 'Spar' advert, Spar being a British convenience store chain, aimed at the person running the email system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spar' looks like the store name but is a ship's pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who administers a mail server is conventionally called by this title, borrowed from the post office.

clue.text: Round mass in pipe unsettled one? Smoker here blew top!

indicators.note: in puts the round mass inside the reworked pipe
unsettled says the letters of pipe are disturbed into another order

parts.note: taken as written
a round thing is shaped like the letter O
M is the physics abbreviation for mass
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pipe smoker who blew their top, asking if one is unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' rearranges PIPE to PPEI, around OM. The smoker is Vesuvius, the volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman city was buried when nearby Vesuvius, a smoking volcano, erupted in AD 79.

clue.text: Sod's Law? Doc for me, suffering terrible hangover!

indicators.note: suffering hints the letters of the phrase are in a bad way and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sufferer blames Sod's Law, the British idea that anything that can go wrong will, and begs the doctor for a hangover cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hangover' is not the morning after drinking but something hanging overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword hung by a single hair over Damocles' head, so the idiom names an ever-present threat.

clue.text: Mum succeeded with second period in therapy

parts.note: ma is a word for mother
S is the genealogy abbreviation for succeeded
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Mum got through a second period of treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing and kneading the muscles is a form of physical treatment.

clue.text: Two tons on farm transport

parts.note: a wain is a farm wagon

explanation.surface: A farm cart carrying a couple of tons.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old word for a pair, as in 'never the twain shall meet'.

clue.text: Organ for example taken in by Royal Academy student

indicators.note: taken in by means the abbreviation is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: RA stands for the Royal Academy of Arts
EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: An organ, given as an example, is accepted by a Royal Academy student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' is not a body part, and the answer is not 'royal' but a small portable reed organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A small portable reed instrument of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries is known by this name.

clue.text: Sober sailors ring us after rough time

indicators.note: after puts the ring and us behind the reworked time

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, so sailors give ABS

indicators.note: rough says the letters of time are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Sailors, sober now, after a rough time on board, ring home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sober' here means abstaining from drink; 'rough' is the anagram signal and 'after' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sober in habits, especially one avoiding drink, is described with this formal adjective.

clue.text: Appropriate to include new and shocking report

indicators.note: to include says the first piece takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: to bag something is to appropriate or seize it

explanation.surface: It seems apt to put something new and shocking in a news report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, seize.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden loud explosion is a startling noise, so a shocking report in the sense of a sharp sound.

clue.text: Writer takes unpleasantly serious direction

parts.note: stern means severe, forbidding
E for east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: An author adopts a grimly serious line.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth-century novelist Laurence Sterne is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Cross, having endless pain in face

indicators.note: in places the shortened pain inside the face

parts.note: the face of a clock or watch is its dial

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for pain is dropped

parts.note: agony is severe pain

explanation.surface: Someone grimacing, crossly, with pain showing on their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like annoyed but means crosswise; 'endless' cuts AGONY to AGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A line running crosswise from corner to corner, slanting across, is a synonym of cross in that sense.

clue.text: Male in CIA put up notice that guarantees good time

indicators.note: in puts the male inside the reversed letters
put up in a down clue means the letters are written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
a tom is a male cat
to clock something is slang for to notice it

explanation.surface: A man in the CIA put up a notice promising everyone a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses in a down clue; 'notice' is the slang verb, to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: This device keeps extremely accurate time from atomic vibrations, so good timekeeping is assured.

clue.text: Greeks initially beat back a bloodsucker

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of Greeks
back means the word for beat is written right to left

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: The Greeks first fought off a vampire-like creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat back' looks like repel, but 'back' reverses TAN to NAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Many small biting flies of this kind feed on blood, so they are an example of a bloodsucker.

clue.text: Change in mood perhaps in 50 consumed by disease

indicators.note: consumed by puts the numeral inside the disease

parts.note: an infection is a disease caught from germs
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A mood swing in a patient eaten up by illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mood' is the grammatical mood of a verb, not a feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, altering a word's ending for mood, tense or case is this kind of change; mood is one example.

clue.text: Distressed hill folk spread out newly-mown grass

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
men means people or folk
to ted is to spread hay out to dry

explanation.surface: Hill people, upset, scatter freshly cut grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone made to suffer greatly is anguished, a strong form of being distressed.

clue.text: Charming Charlie in with tradesmen

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the word with

parts.note: taken as written
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a craft is a trade, and its members collectively

explanation.surface: A charming man called Charlie gets on well with tradespeople.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' is the noun, casting charms.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting magic spells, the act of charming in its old sense, is sorcery.

clue.text: A sinner at last was in church for cleansing service!

indicators.note: in puts these pieces inside the church
at last picks the final letter of sinner

explanation.surface: A sinner was finally in church to be cleansed of sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleansing service' suggests a church rite, but is a place to wash a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that washes vehicles offers a cleaning service for motorists.

clue.text: Great moves by wingers from Ards in blinder

indicators.note: moves says the letters of great are moved about
wingers from takes the outside letters of Ards

explanation.surface: A footballer for Ards, a Northern Ireland club, makes great moves down the wing in a blinder of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blinder' sounds like a superb game but means something that blinds.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas makes the eyes stream so painfully that it temporarily blinds people.

clue.text: Ultimate in consular assistance for Sally

indicators.note: ultimate in picks the last letter of consular

parts.note: aid is help or assistance

explanation.surface: Someone named Sally gets the best consular help abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' is not a woman's name but a sudden military sortie.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden charge out against an enemy, much like a surprise attack.

clue.text: Artist in comeback managed act with lion

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac

indicators.note: in comeback says the word for managed is turned back to front

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
to do is to act or perform

explanation.surface: A performer in a comeback show runs an act with a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in comeback' turns RAN into NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci, painter of the Mona Lisa, is a famous example of an artist.

clue.text: What was tender of Italians entertaining British stars?

indicators.note: entertaining means the old currency hosts the letter inside it

parts.note: the lira was Italy's legal tender before the euro

explanation.surface: A question about which Italian once entertained British film stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' means money, not gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: This constellation, the scales of the zodiac, is a group of stars.

clue.text: Passing remarks about Republican circle

indicators.note: about means the remarks go round the letter

parts.note: an obit, or obituary, gives remarks on someone's passing

explanation.surface: Offhand comments about a Republican circle of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing remarks' looks like casual comments, but it means words on a death.
explanation.definitionFit: A path round a planet or star is a circling route, so the word can stand for circle.

clue.text: Means business

definitions.meaning: a means or instrument by which something is done
a firm providing a service, such as a travel or advertising firm

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the instrument through which something happens and a company offering a service.

clue.text: Pretty Woman's noisy scene finally cut

indicators.note: finally cut means the end letter of the noisy scene is removed

parts.note: a babel is a confused din of voices, after the tower of Babel

explanation.surface: A scene from the film Pretty Woman, a loud one, has been cut from the final edit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty Woman' suggests the film, but is simply an attractive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe is informal slang for an attractive young woman.

clue.text: Charge at goal line recklessly

indicators.note: recklessly suggests the letters of at goal line are thrown about wildly

explanation.surface: A footballer charges at the goal line without care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a rush on goal but is an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusation, especially one not yet proved, is a charge in the legal sense.

clue.text: Opposition wants taxes introduced to an island

indicators.note: introduced to says the taxes are put inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
tithes were taxes of a tenth paid to the church

explanation.surface: Political opposition to a plan to impose taxes on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposition' looks political but means a direct contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct contrast or opposite of something is its exact opposite, which is the sense of opposition here.

clue.text: Nobleman expected to receive king

indicators.note: to receive means the first word takes the letter inside

parts.note: due means expected, as in the train is due
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A peer anticipated a visit from the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of the British peerage, so a nobleman.
